verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属耶和华。
verses.en: A psalm of David.The Lord owns the earth and all it contains,the world and all who live in it.

verses.zh: 他把地建立在海上，安定在大水之上。
verses.en: For he set its foundation upon the seas,and established[NOTE:1] it upon the ocean currents.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 24. The psalmist affirms the universal kingship of the sovereign creator, reminds his people that only the morally pure are qualified to worship him, and celebrates his splendor as a mighty warrior king.
The prefixed verbal form is understood as a preterite, referring to the creation of the world.

verses.zh: 谁能登耶和华的山？谁能站在他的圣所？
verses.en: Who is allowed to ascend[NOTE:1] the mountain of the Lord?[NOTE:2] Who may go up to his holy dwelling place?
notes: He…established it upon the ocean currents. The description reflects ancient Israelite prescientific cosmology, which is based on outward appearances. The language also suggests that God’s creative work involved the subjugation of chaos, symbolized by the sea.
The imperfects in v. 3 are modal, expressing potential or permission.

verses.zh: 就是手洁心清、不向虚妄、起誓不怀诡诈的人。
verses.en: The one whose deeds are blamelessand whose motives are pure,[NOTE:1] who does not lie,[NOTE:2] or make promises with no intention of keeping them.[NOTE:3]
notes: In this context the Lord’s mountain probably refers to Zion/Jerusalem (see Isa 2:2-3).
Heb “the innocent of hands and the pure of heart.” The “hands” allude to one’s actions, the “heart” to one’s thought life and motives.

Heb “who does not lift up for emptiness my life.” The first person pronoun on נַפְשִׁי (nafshi, “my life”) makes little sense here; many medieval Hebrew mss support the ancient versions in reading a third person pronoun “his.” The idiom “lift the life” here means to “long for” or “desire strongly.” In this context (note the reference to an oath in the following line) “emptiness” probably refers to speech (see Ps 12:2).

verses.zh: 他必蒙耶和华赐福，又蒙救他的　神使他成义。
verses.en: Such godly people are rewarded by the Lord,[NOTE:1] and vindicated by the God who delivers them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and does not swear an oath deceitfully.”

Heb “he (the righteous individual described in v. 4) lifts up a blessing from the Lord.” The singular subject is representative here, as v. 6 makes clear. The referent (godly people like the individual in v. 4) has been specified in the translation for clarity. The imperfect verbal form is generalizing; such people are typically rewarded for their deeds.

verses.zh: 这是寻求耶和华的族类，是寻求你面的雅各。（细拉）
verses.en: Such purity characterizes the people who seek his favor,Jacob’s descendants, who pray to him.[NOTE:1] (Selah)
notes: “and vindication from the God of his deliverance.”

verses.zh: 众城门哪，你们要抬起头来！永久的门户，你们要被举起！那荣耀的王将要进来！
verses.en: Look up,[NOTE:1] you gates.Rise up,[NOTE:2] you eternal doors.Then the majestic king[NOTE:3] will enter.[NOTE:4]
notes: This verse presents a somewhat idealized view of Jacob’s descendants as devoted worshipers of the Lord.tn Heb “this [is the] generation of the ones seeking him, the ones seeking your face, Jacob.” To “seek the Lord’s face” means to seek his favor through prayer (see 2 Sam 21:1; Pss 27:8; 105:4).
Heb “lift up your heads.” The gates of the Lord’s dwelling place are here personified. The idiom “lift up the head” often means “be confident, bold” (see Judg 8:28; Job 10:15; Ps 83:2; Zech 1:21).

verses.zh: 荣耀的王是谁呢？就是有力有能的耶和华，在战场上有能的耶和华！
verses.en: Who is this majestic king?[NOTE:1] The Lord who is strong and mighty.The Lord who is mighty in battle.
notes: Following the imperatives of the preceding lines, the prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose or result.

verses.zh: 众城门哪，你们要抬起头来！永久的门户，你们要把头抬起！那荣耀的王将要进来！
verses.en: Look up, you gates.Rise up, you eternal doors.Then the majestic king will enter.

verses.zh: 荣耀的王是谁呢？万军之耶和华，他是荣耀的王！（细拉）
verses.en: Who is this majestic king?The Lord of Heaven’s Armies.[NOTE:1] He is the majestic king. (Selah)
notes: Who is this majestic king? Perhaps the personified gates/doors ask this question, in response to the command given in v. 7.
